subject: MPA: Pilot Retail evaluation dataset exchange & escrow sprint plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@pilotretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MPA: Pilot Retail evaluation dataset exchange & escrow sprint plan

Hi Sarah —

Great to connect on the call earlier. Per our discussion I attached a starter Mutual Action Plan (MPA) that lays out milestones for the eval dataset, prompt pack handoff, and the conditional escrow and takedown timeline. High level:

- Week 0 (this week): sign MPA + security questionnaire kickoff
- Week 1: ephemeral prompt pack (sandbox) delivered to Pilot Retail engineers (S3 link + checksum)
- Week 2: Acceptance tests (10k queries, defined acceptance set)
- Week 4: Canary in production with Redwood routing; limited token budget
- Week 8: Final handback or extended license (per agreed usage constraints)

A few notes on usage constraints: prompt pack is provided for evaluation only; no re-distribution; ephemeral sandboxes expire at the end of the sprint window. We propose an escrow window of 90 days for audit/forensics, followed by staged deletion tests.

Attached: MPA-Redwood-PilotRetail-v1.pdf (draft). I also included a short checklist for acceptance criteria. Can you confirm: procurement timeline, security contact for the questionnaire, and whether your team needs a hashed ingest bundle (SHA256) or a signed transmission?

Thanks — happy to adjust the milestones.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the clear draft and the call recap. We like the sprint structure and the escrow idea. A few asks from our side:

- Security: please fill out our standard questionnaire (I copied procurement). Their security contact is Aileen Park (external partner) who will run the SOC2/arch review.
- Legal/Procurement: procurement will need a Statement of Work and the license language for ephemeral access spelled out (tokens, redistrib restrictions).
- Delivery: hashed bundle (SHA256) is preferred, and we will also require an SFTP + signed receipt for the initial ingest.

Tentative timeline: procurement needs ~2 weeks for review once legal has the MPA and SOW. Can Redwood provide a version of the MPA with the explicit acceptance test matrix included (pass/fail thresholds + sample queries)?

Cc'ing procurement so they can coordinate next steps.

Best,
Sarah

Subject: RE: MPA: Pilot Retail evaluation dataset exchange & escrow sprint plan

Ben / team —

Quick internal note before we send an updated MPA to Pilot:

Acceptance criteria suggestions (we should bake into the MPA):
- Accuracy bucket: >= 92% on curated acceptance set (5k items)
- Latency: p95 < 220ms for generation endpoint during canary traffic (token budget limited)
- Safety gate: zero high-confidence PII leakage incidents in 1k random audits

Access and usage constraints to include explicitly:
- Ephemeral sandbox: 30-day access, auto-expire, no export of raw test prompts/data
- Token budget: pilot capped at 1.5M tokens total across the sprint unless otherwise agreed
- Escrow: archive stored in encrypted S3 for 90 days; retrieval only with signed request and audit log

I'll draft the matrix and the short legal-friendly bullets for the license clauses. Priyom, can you prepare the ephemeral-access doc (how key rotation works, audit log retention) and attach?

-Kim

- Day 3-9: Acceptance tests run by Pilot Retail with Redwood remote support

- Monday 2025-11-10 EOB: Redwood to circulate redlined MPA with the legal language and final SOW stub
- Tuesday 2025-11-11: Procurement call to agree SOW and finalize token budget
- Wed 2025-11-12: Secure transfer of encrypted prompt pack (if signed)
- Thu 2025-11-13: Acceptance tests begin
